title: יהושע פרק 12
english: Now these are the kings of the land, which the children of Israel smote, and possessed their land on the other side Jordan toward the rising of the sun, from the river Arnon unto mount Hermon, and all the plain on the east:

Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, and ruled from Aroer, which is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and from the middle of the river, and from half Gilead, even unto the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon;
And from the plain to the sea of Chinneroth on the east, and unto the sea of the plain, even the salt sea on the east, the way to Bethjeshimoth; and from the south, under Ashdothpisgah:
And the coast of Og king of Bashan, which was of the remnant of the giants, that dwelt at Ashtaroth and at Edrei,
And reigned in mount Hermon, and in Salcah, and in all Bashan, unto the border of the Geshurites and the Maachathites, and half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon.

Them did Moses the servant of the Lord and the children of Israel smite: and Moses the servant of the Lord gave it for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh.

And these are the kings of the country which Joshua and the children of Israel smote on this side Jordan on the west, from Baalgad in the valley of Lebanon even unto the mount Halak, that goeth up to Seir; which Joshua gave unto the tribes of Israel for a possession according to their divisions;

In the mountains, and in the valleys, and in the plains, and in the springs, and in the wilderness, and in the south country; the Hittites, the Amorites, and the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites:
The king of Jericho, one; the king of Ai, which is beside Bethel, one;
The king of Jerusalem, one; the king of Hebron, one;
The king of Jarmuth, one; the king of Lachish, one;
The king of Eglon, one; the king of Gezer, one;
The king of Debir, one; the king of Geder, one;
The king of Hormah, one; the king of Arad, one;
The king of Libnah, one; the king of Adullam, one;
The king of Makkedah, one; the king of Bethel, one;
The king of Tappuah, one; the king of Hepher, one;
The king of Aphek, one; the king of Lasharon, one;
The king of Madon, one; the king of Hazor, one;
The king of Shimronmeron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;
The king of Taanach, one; the king of Megiddo, one;
The king of Kedesh, one; the king of Jokneam of Carmel, one;
The king of Dor in the coast of Dor, one; the king of the nations of Gilgal, one;
The king of Tirzah, one: all the kings thirty and one.
ai_explanation: השורה מונה את מלכי הארץ שניצחו בני־ישראל וירשו את ארצותיהם בעבר הירדן המזרחי; התחום הוא מנחל ארנון עד הר חרמון וכל הערבה ממזרח.
מדובר בארצו של סיחון מלך האמורי, שישב בחשבון והשתרעה ממערך שעריו ועד ערעור שעל שפת נחל ארנון, כולל השטח התוחם בתוך הנחל שהיה ראוי לשימוש, חצי הגלעד ועד נחל יבוק שהוא גבול בני עמון.
הערבה נמתחה עד שפתה הדרום‑מזרחית של ים כנרת וכללה את עמק הירדן והשטחים הסמוכים לו; והגיעה גם לשפתו הצפון‑מזרחית של ים המלח בסביבת דרך בית הישמות, וכן למקום מדרום לים המלח שמתחת לאשדות הפסגה.
גבולו של עוּג מלך הבשן היה שריד מן היתֶר־הרפאים, והוא ישב בערי הבירה עשתרות ואדרעי.
עוּג שלט בהר חרמון, בסַלְכָּה ובכל הבשן — החלק הצפוני של עבר הירדן — עד גבולות הגשור והמעכתי; וחצי הגלעד הוזכר כבר כגבול של סיחון מלך־חשבון.
משה עבד ה' וּבְנֵי ישראל הכו את עמי האזור האלה, ומשה נתן את ארצם לירושת ראובן, לגדי ולחצי שבט מנשה; זה מסכם את כיבוש עבר הירדן המזרחי ומי שהתיישב בו.
אלה מלכי הארץ אשר הכה יהושע ובני ישראל בעֵבר הירדן המערבי: הטווח הוא מבעל־גד בבקעת הלבנון ועד ההר החלק העולה שעירה; יהושע נתן את הארץ לשבטים לפי מחלקותיהם.
הכיבוש נעשה בהר, בשפלה, בערבה, באשדות, במדבר ובנגב, והעמים שישבו שם היו החתי, האמורי, הכנעני, הפריזי, החווי והיבוסי — אלה המקומות והעמים שנכללים ברשימה.
כאן מתחיל פירוט המלכים שנכבשו; ברוב המקרים כל מלך שלט בעיר אחת וסביבתה, והרשימה נמנית פר פר כדי להדגיש את גדולת יהושע וסדר הכיבושים. מֶלֶךְ יְרִיחוֹ — אחד. מֶלֶךְ הָעַי (מצד בית־אל) — אחד.
מֶלֶךְ יְרוּשָׁלַים — אחד; מֶלֶךְ חֶבְרוֹן — אחד.
מֶלֶךְ יַרְמוּת — אחד; מֶלֶךְ לָכִישׁ — אחד.
מֶלֶךְ עֶגְלוֹן — אחד; מֶלֶךְ גֶּזֶר — אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך דביר – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך חרמה – אחד, ומלך ערד – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך לבנה – אחד, ומלך עֲדֻלָּם – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך מקדה – אחד, ומלך בית אל – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך תפוח – אחד, ומלך חֵפֶר – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך אפק – אחד, ומלך השרון – כנראה נקודה מסוימת ולא כל אזור השרון – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך מדון – אחד, ומלך חצור – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך שִׁמְרוֹן מְרֹאון – גם הוא מאימפריית המלכים שבצפון – אחד, ומלך אַכְשָׁף – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך תענך – אחד, ומלך מגידו – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך קדש – אחד, ומלך יקנעם לכרמל – באזור הכרמל – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך דור לנפת דור – אחד, ומלך גוים בגלגל – אחד.
השטיינזלץ מציין שמלך תרצה – אחד, והוא מוסיף שסך כל המלכים ששלטו בארץ כנען לפני שיהושע שבר את מערך הממלכות וכבש את עריהם הוא שלושים ואחד.
ai_explanation_en: This verse introduces the list as the kings whose lands Israel defeated and then occupied on the east side of the Jordan, specifying the region from the Arnon stream up to Mount Hermon and including the eastern plain (the Arabah).

Steinsaltz explains that Sihon’s domain centered on Heshbon and included Aroer on the bank of the Arnon, the usable stretch in the middle of that river, and half of Gilead extending to the Jabbok River, which is the border of the Ammonites.

He clarifies that the territory extended from the plain to the southeastern shore of the Sea of Chinneroth (the Sea of Galilee), included the Jordan valley and adjacent areas, and reached to the northern-eastern shore of the Salt Sea (Dead Sea) via the road to Beth-jeshimoth, as well as the region south of the Dead Sea under Ashdoth‑Pisgah noted in the Torah.
This line identifies Og king of Bashan as a remnant of the Rephaim (giants) whose strongholds were at Ashtaroth and Edrei.

Steinsaltz states that Og ruled Mount Hermon, Salcah and all of Bashan — the northern part of the Transjordan — up to the borders of the small northeastern polities Geshur and Maacah, and included the half‑Gilead already described as Sihon’s border.

He notes that Moses and the Israelites defeated these peoples, and Moses allotted their land as an inheritance to the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and the half‑tribe of Manasseh; this serves as a summary of the conquest east of the Jordan.

This introduces the kings defeated on the west side of the Jordan by Joshua and the Israelites, giving the geographic range from Baal‑gad in the Lebanon valley to Mount Halak near Seir, and states that Joshua allotted these lands to the tribes according to their divisions.

Steinsaltz lists the types of terrain conquered — mountains, lowlands, plains, springs, wilderness and Negev — and the peoples who lived there (Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites), indicating the areas Israel took and the nations displaced.

He explains that the list now gives individual defeated kings, some ruling larger territories and some only a city and its environs, enumerated to honor Joshua’s achievements; Jericho is listed first as one, and Ai (noted as beside Bethel to distinguish its small site or another Ai) is listed as one.
This simply repeats the list entries: the king of Jerusalem — one; the king of Hebron — one.
Continues the concise list of defeated rulers: the king of Jarmuth — one; the king of Lachish — one.
And again the list continues in the same terse manner: the king of Eglon — one; the king of Gezer — one.
Steinsaltz simply notes that the king of Debir was one; the king of Geder was one, recording a single ruler for each city.
He records that the king of Hormah was one and the king of Arad was one, i.e., each city had a single king listed.
He states that the king of Libnah was one and the king of Adullam was one, again noting one ruler for each place.
He records that the king of Makkedah was one and the king of Bethel was one, indicating a single king in each city.
He notes that the king of Tappuah was one and the king of Hepher was one, each having one king.
He records the king of Aphek as one and the king of Lasharon as one, adding that 'Lasharon' likely denotes a specific locality rather than the whole Sharon region.
He notes that the king of Madon was one and the king of Hazor was one, each listed as a single monarch.
He records the king of Shimron Meron as one and the king of Achshaph as one, commenting that Shimron Meron is among the northern kings.
He states that the king of Taanach was one and the king of Megiddo was one, each city having a single king.
He records that the king of Kedesh was one and the king of Jokneam of the Carmel was one, specifying Jokneam as being in the Carmel area.
He notes that the king of Dor by the coast of Dor was one and the king of the nations at Gilgal was one, each listed as one ruler.

He records that the king of Tirzah was one and explains that the total number of kings who ruled in the land of Canaan before Joshua broke the system of kingdoms and conquered their cities was thirty-one.

did_you_know.text_en: The Arnon River is repeatedly used in the Bible as a boundary; Sihon ruled in the Transjordan area around its key towns.

did_you_know.text_en: The Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea are two very different lakes: the Galilee is freshwater and used for drinking, while the Dead Sea is extremely salty and lies at the lowest land elevation.

did_you_know.text_en: Og king of Bashan is called 'the remnant of the Rephaim' — in the Bible 'Rephaim' sometimes refers to an ancient people or to legendary giants.

did_you_know.text_en: That Moses allotted land to Reuben, Gad and half-Manasseh shows the eastern tribes received territory beyond the Jordan before the full settlement of the west.
